steps.what: List municipal documents with no filing place.
Plan safekeeping and filing of municipal documents.
Direct computerization of the remaining paper series.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store lists every municipal document series that has no filing place or safekeeping owner. The registry clerk plans which series to computerise and which stay on paper. A gap list does not move a file. The clerk directs each move, and only then does the records screen update the location.
tasks.previous_blocker: Series lists lived in personal notes, so a gap was visible only to the clerk who remembered it.
tasks.enabler_now: A records screen can list series with an empty location field. The plan itself is still the clerk's.
tasks.still_hard: Retention periods and which series may leave paper follow national rules the screen does not know.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk knows which series the council still asks for in the original, and which fire or flood risk matters in this building.

ambition.what: Review safekeeping for the small record series each quarter, not only the series that already have a complaint.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends the week on series that have no owner. Location updates no longer wait for a spare afternoon.

reach.task: File and retrieve a named item from a location rule.
reach.learn: A location rule can place a file. Retention of a municipal series stays with the clerk.

evidence.claim: A records screen can list series whose location field is empty. Moving a series is a separate instruction.
Filing location is not a decision about a person's rights. No score of clerks is added, and the job digest says staff dashboards that monitor people need works-council consent.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The desk is a European municipal court registry and licensing counter. The sentence uses US public-sector wording and is read as the local court, council, or permit this municipality actually issues.

Fields: Series id, title, current location, and medium, produced by the records screen. A series with no title is skipped. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the clerk finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the location field already on {DOCS} before building a second inventory.
unknowns: Which series the municipality must keep on paper.
Who may direct a move besides this clerk.
research_questions: How many series have an empty location today?
Which retention rules are written down?

already_counted.description: The clerk still writes the safekeeping plan.
The clerk still directs which series move.

incremental.description: The clerk adds a new series title to the location list.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If half the series have no title in the store, the clerk types those by hand and the saving falls toward the low end. A clean location field keeps the high end.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Examine legal documents against court procedures.

steps.what: Examine legal documents for listed court procedures.

loop.input: the filing and the written procedure list
loop.output: a gap list naming each missing item
loop.check: every gap cites a procedure id that is on the list
loop.stop: stop when a required procedure id is not on the list
loop.why_not_simpler: a filing is free text, so a fixed form cannot see a missing exhibit

steps.what: Judge adherence where the procedure list is silent.
Accept the filing or return it to the filer.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} register checks a submitted filing against the written procedure list and names each missing item. The registry clerk judges adherence where the list is silent, then accepts the filing or returns it. The list does not decide the case. A missing procedure id stops the check and the clerk reads the filing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedure lists sat in binders, so each clerk applied the pages they remembered.
tasks.enabler_now: A written list with ids can be checked item by item. The accept-or-return decision stays with the clerk.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual exhibits and late amendments do not match a fixed list.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk sees when a missing page is a copy problem and when it changes what the court can hear.
tasks.altitude: The clerk's week moves from hunting the procedure page to the filings the list cannot settle. The decision to accept a filing does not move.

reach.task: Check an application for the fields the form requires.
reach.learn: A missing field is a rule. Accepting a court filing is a different decision and stays here.

evidence.claim: A procedure list with ids can mark a missing exhibit. Free text that matches no id has to be read by a person.

Accepting a filing can affect a party's position. The job digest says a solely automated decision with legal effect is not allowed unless a legal ground applies, and a narrow procedure check is not that decision. The clerk accepts or returns the filing.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The desk is a European municipal court registry and licensing counter. The sentence uses US public-sector wording and is read as the local court, council, or permit this municipality actually issues.

Fields: Procedure id, document type, and party name, produced by the court procedure list and the filing. A filing with no party name is not checked. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the clerk finishes it by hand.
Native check: Store the procedure list in the existing {DOCS} library before writing a new checker.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the clerk.
unknowns: Who may accept a filing in this court.
Whether the procedure list is complete and dated.
research_questions: Which filings are returned today for a missing exhibit?

already_counted.description: The clerk still judges filings the list does not settle.
The clerk still accepts or returns the filing.

incremental.description: The clerk adds a procedure id when the court changes a rule.

approvals.approved_version: gap-list id and the accept-or-return choice shown to the clerk

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the procedure list is incomplete, most filings fall through to the clerk and the saving stays near the low end. A current list with ids keeps the high end.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record dispositions, orders, and fee arrangements.

steps.what: Read case dispositions from the judge's note.

loop.check: each field quotes a line in the note
loop.stop: stop when the note has no disposition line
loop.why_not_simpler: handwritten notes are not a fixed form

steps.what: Record those court orders in the register.
Record arrangements for payment of court fees.
Spot-check one posted fee row the next morning.

tasks.design: A draft reads the judge's signed note into disposition, order, and fee fields, and the registry clerk accepts that extract before anything is stored. {WORKFLOW} then records the court orders and {ERP} records the fee arrangement from the tariff. The screen does not change the judge's outcome. A note with no disposition line is typed by the clerk.
tasks.previous_blocker: The clerk retyped the note into the register and the fee book, and a bad copy was found late.
tasks.enabler_now: A signed note with a disposition line can be copied into fields. The clerk still accepts the copy.
tasks.still_hard: Handwritten notes and outcomes given only in the hearing are not fields yet.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk knows the judge's usual wording and when a fee line is a payment plan rather than a sum due today.
tasks.altitude: The clerk stops retyping clear notes. The right to record what the judge decided does not move to the screen.

reach.task: Record a payment against the amount the customer handed over.
reach.learn: A fee row must match the tariff and the judge's note. The clerk still accepts the row.

evidence.claim: Fields that quote a signed note can be stored as a record. A note with no disposition line cannot be stored that way.

The job digest says justice administration is high-risk under the EU AI Act from 2 December 2027, and narrow procedural copying falls outside it. This step copies an outcome the judge already made. It does not choose a sentence. Order-call retention from another job is not this record.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The desk is a European municipal court registry and licensing counter. The sentence uses US public-sector wording and is read as the local court, council, or permit this municipality actually issues.

Fields: Case id, disposition line, order type, and fee amount or plan, produced by the judge's signed note. The tariff id comes from {ERP}. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the clerk finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the case register's existing outcome fields before adding a new store.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the clerk.
The extract is not a transcript of a call, and it does not stand in for any duty to keep recordings.
unknowns: Whether judges already sign a structured minute.
Who may correct a posted fee row.
research_questions: What share of notes are still handwriting?
Which fee plans the tariff cannot express?

already_counted.description: The clerk still accepts the extract from the note.
The clerk still spot-checks a posted fee row.

incremental.description: The clerk maps a new order type onto the register fields.

approvals.approved_version: note id and the disposition fields shown to the clerk
accepted extract id and the order rows about to be stored
accepted extract id and the fee rows about to be stored

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If most notes are handwriting, the clerk types them and the saving stays near the low end. Typed notes with a disposition line keep the high end.

tasks.short: Answer inquiries on dates, warrants, and fines.

steps.what: Show trial dates, adjournments, and witness fees.
Answer inquiries about warrants, summonses, or subpoenas.
Send a written reply that cites the register.

tasks.design: The {CALENDAR} and the case register show a published trial date, adjournment, or witness fee. The registry clerk answers inquiries about warrants, summonses, subpoenas, and fines from the live register. A written reply cites that row and the clerk sends it. A machine reply, if one is ever shown, must say it is a machine. The desk does not invent a warrant status.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dates and warrant questions arrived in the same phone queue, and the clerk looked each one up from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: A published date is a field. Warrant status is not safe to read out from a stale card.
tasks.still_hard: People describe a case without a number, and a fine question can turn into advice about paying it.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk hears when a caller is a party, a journalist, or someone who should not be told that a warrant exists.

ambition.what: Answer a published trial date for a caller who only has a case number, the same day, including callers who now wait on the warrant queue.

tasks.altitude: Published dates leave the phone call. The clerk keeps every question about a warrant, a summons, or whether a fine is still due.

reach.role: Hotel, Motel, and Resort Desk Clerks
reach.task: Answer a question about a stay from the booking record.
reach.learn: A date on the record can be read out. A warrant question is not that, and stays with this clerk.

evidence.claim: A register can show a hearing date that is already published. It cannot safely state a warrant from an incomplete question.

The job digest says that from 2 August 2026 a chat that is a machine must say so, and an answer desk must hand off when the question becomes advice. This clerk answers warrant and fine questions. No call recording is added, because the digest says recording needs works-council consent.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The desk is a European municipal court registry and licensing counter. The sentence uses US public-sector wording and is read as the local court, council, or permit this municipality actually issues.

Fields: Case id, hearing date, adjournment flag, and published witness-fee amount, produced by the case register. Warrant status is not a field on the public card. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the clerk finishes it by hand.
Native check: Show the date from the existing case screen before adding a chat.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the clerk.
unknowns: Whether the counter already records calls.
research_questions: What share of calls are only a date question?
Who may be told that a warrant exists?

already_counted.description: The clerk still answers warrant and summons questions.
The clerk still sends the written reply.

incremental.description: The clerk updates the public date card when a hearing type changes.

approvals.approved_version: case id, date card, and the reply text shown to the clerk

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If callers rarely have a case number, the clerk still searches and the saving stays near the low end. Clear case numbers and published dates keep the high end.

role.altitude: The clerk still plans safekeeping, accepts a filing, and answers a warrant question. Location lists, fee rows, and published dates leave the hour.
reach: Library assistants file a named item from a location rule, and this desk learns which odd file the person still fetches.
Hotel desk clerks answer a date from the booking, and this desk learns when the question has become advice.
skills_to_grow: Tell a published court date from a question about a warrant or a fine.
Read a fee row back to the tariff before the disposition is filed.
role.ambitious_version: A resident who asks a published trial date gets it the same day, and a warrant question still waits for the clerk.
